title: I Took the Indoor-Playground Sock Policy to the Manager's Barefoot Niece

parts.text: I paid socks-required at 10:16 a.m. and the manager's niece was already on the slides barefoot. The door sign said: GRIP SOCKS. ALL FEET. STAFF KIDS TOO. I was thirty-four, parent, holding a pair I had just bought. Manager Gail waved. "Nieces are home." I photographed the sign, the receipt, and the bare feet on the slide. Then I logged a skip. At 10:24 regional asked why Gail's niece was on a no-sock still. I asked once, then I documented twice. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Regional can see bare feet on the slide against the grip-sock sign and my receipt.

social.video_title: The manager's niece slid barefoot under a sock sign — Part 1/2
social.description: Indoor playground, bought socks, and a niece on the slide. I logged the skip. Would you have photographed the feet?

parts.text: Gail called it family until regional asked for the still. I printed the skip, the photo, and the sign. Socks went on. Gail's niece gripped like everyone else and told the desk family was always about optics. Optics is a word managers use when a niece exists. Sock policy now has a second line: NIECES ARE FEET. I keep the receipt. Gail sells socks to her own. The slides finally look like a park, not a house. The room sounds like a room again, not a title. Petty is a word people use when their name is on the ticket.

social.description: Skip still, socked niece, and a second line. Was family ever barefoot?
